doc.title: Emile Barnes and Paul Barnes Interview, 1959-10-01

title: Lessons from Lorenzo Tio and Tartarella
summary: Paul describes his sax lessons with Tio, who was always tipsy, and advice from Tartarella in the Navy.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: I don't want to interrupt you, but I don't want to miss this about you took some lessons from Lorenzo Teo, you say. He helped you with the sax or clarinet or both?
Oh no, with the saxophone. With the sax. I actually didn't take any lessons from anyone on the clarinet. You see, no more than Miele gave me.

Helping you with the clarinet. But I got some great advice from Tartarella from the Boston Conservatory of Music when I was in the Navy. Yes. And I would practice and he'd sit down and tell me the different things and he'd see to it that I would smooth out my tones and so forth. It made quite a great difference in my playing.
I was wondering about Teo since he's not living of course and we never found very much information about Teo. Do you remember much about how he played and what he told you when he helped you or what

he was like? For his playing, actually I think that he was one of the greatest players we had here at that time. Lorenzo Teo, his tone and all was so smooth. But mostly when I would take lessons with Lorenzo Teo, he was always tipsy. Sometimes I couldn't get my lesson. He was always tipsy. Somebody told me he liked wine a lot.
Is that it or what? I didn't know.
I never know what he drank. But he stayed high.

Oh well, something else. As I say, I know almost nothing about him. Some people told me that it might have been his father or his uncle they were talking about, the old Lorenzo or Papa, that they talked a little bit with an accent, a French accent. Did young Lorenzo still have a French accent? He did. He did too.
At that time, he the young fella, he did have a French accent. But he taught me and Bonnie Bigard taking lessons from the Teos also, but from the daddy, I think.
I don't think it was Lorenzo, but he was from the daddy. Anyway, when Piro and them returned in 1924, the Tuxedo band came out. And you heard some of the recordings that we made.
